About the book

“She told them Friday because, for one bright second, they had all looked relieved to see her.”

From the opening of Act One

Lena has spent six weeks moving a lender’s loans to a new system. Two dates have already slipped. On Monday morning the balances finally match, and the whole room is waiting for one word.

She gives it to them: Friday.

What she meant to say first was the condition. The new system still has to prove it knows the 214 customers who were promised that nothing would leave their accounts while their hardship cases were reviewed. Some of them planned their rent around that promise.

Over one long week, Lena has to answer to a sponsor who needs a date, an assurance lead who will not let a sentence claim more than the evidence, an operations manager who is running out of people, and a sister who needs her for two hours on Saturday morning and has heard “I’ll be there” before.

A warm, sharp and often funny novel about what we promise in meetings, and who pays for it.
